events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
An active monsoon pattern will continue to bring scattered to
numerous, locally heavy, showers and isolated to scattered
thunderstorms across portions of Yap State through this evening.
Frequent lightning, wind gusts to 30 knots, and choppy seas can be
expected with thunderstorms. Inter-island travel will be hazardous
through at least this evening. Then, a relative lull in shower
coverage is expected after midnight as showers and thunderstorms
weaken. However, shower and thunderstorm coverage is expected to
increase once again on Wednesday with locally heavy rainfall
expected. Due to saturated conditions, mudslides will be possible
where the heaviest rain occurs. Residents across Yap State should
monitor local forecasts and heed advice of emergency managers when
heavy rainfall occurs.

events.summary:
At 1256 AM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 8 miles north of Rushville to 8 miles north of
Ellsworth. Movement was southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Gordon, Rushville, Hay Springs, Clinton, Watson Lake, Big Hill,
Dipping Vat Meadow, Morgan Lake, Billys Lake, Lone Butte, Highway 27
crossing the Niobrara River, Highway 250 crossing the Niobrara River,
Walgren Lake State Recreation Area, Smith Lake State Wildlife
Management Area, Rock Hill, Bayonne, Intersection of Highway 27 and
Mills Road, Mother Lake, Wickson Lake, and Diamond Lake.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 20 between mile markers 80 and 114.
Highway 250 between mile markers 7 and 48.

events.summary:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 600 AM MST /700 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 1131 PM MST /1231 AM MDT/, River gauge reports indicate a large
flood wave on the Paria River is traveling south from Utah toward
the Arizona border. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Paria River.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Vermilion Cliffs National Monument and Lees Ferry.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
